info.description:
Welcome to the Magicweave Game Developer SDK API.

These endpoints are meant to be consumed directly by client applications (e.g., Unity, Unreal, strictly frontend web clients). All requests must include your `x-client-id` and `x-client-secret` headers to identify your game/project.

**Errors.** Every error response carries a stable machine-readable `error.code` (e.g. `insufficient_balance`, `idempotency_conflict`) alongside the human-readable `detail`. Branch on `error.code`; treat `detail` as display text that may be reworded at any time.

**Retry safety.** Mutating endpoints accept an idempotency key — as an `Idempotency-Key` header on inventory and shop writes, and as an `idempotency_key` body field on `/game` writes. Reuse the same key for every retry of the same logical action and persist it before sending. When a key is omitted where one is accepted, the response carries `x-mw-idempotency-generated: true` and that write is not retry-safe.

**Identify your SDK.** Send `x-mw-sdk: <platform>/<version>` (e.g. `unity/0.3.1`) so the console can show which SDK builds are live and warn you before a breaking change.
info.title: Magicweave SDK & Client APIs

post.description:
Schedule the authenticated player's project account for deletion after a 30-day grace period, and email them a confirmation. Signing in again before the scheduled date cancels it automatically.

Idempotent — calling it again while a deletion is already scheduled returns the existing request and the same date.

This affects the player's account in **this project only**. Their Magicweave Network account and the gems attached to it are shared across every network game and are never touched.

post.description:
Send a stable `Idempotency-Key` header to safely retry the same consume request.

Omit it and the server generates one, the response carries
`x-mw-idempotency-generated: true`, and a retry will apply the
operation a second time.

parameters.description: A stable, caller-generated key that makes this write safe to retry — replaying the same key returns the original result instead of applying the operation twice. Reuse the *same* key for every retry of the same logical action, and persist it before sending so it survives a crash. If omitted, the server generates a random key and this request is NOT retry-safe.
